description: Wigderson Algorithm A for promised 3-colorable simple graphs, with deterministic ties and source-faithful color stride.

source.title: Improving the Performance Guarantee for Approximate Graph Coloring
source.reference: JACM 30(4), 729-735, Section 2, Algorithm A and Theorem 2.1
source.chapter: Encyclopedia of Algorithms, Chapter 170: Graph Coloring
source.rights: Clean-room ports based on the mathematical method; no source code, examples, figures, or protected prose reused.

input.graph: Simple undirected graph with vertices 0..n-1; each edge appears once as u<v. The source promise is 3-colorability.

contract.threshold: floor(sqrt(original_n)); compare against the current maximum degree throughout
contract.selection: Maximum current degree, then smallest vertex ID
contract.neighborhood_coloring: Induced subgraph on current neighbors; BFS components rooted by ascending vertex ID, scan neighbors ascending, side labels i and i+1
contract.center_color_and_stride: Assign i+2 to the center, delete the closed neighborhood, then advance i by exactly two as printed in Algorithm A
contract.residual_coloring: Ascending vertex ID, sequential first-fit using the smallest available label at least i
contract.output: [highest_color_id,color_0,...,color_(n-1)] as one-byte unsigned values; labels are one-based
contract.errors: Malformed/out-of-promise selected neighborhood returns -1; null or insufficient output returns -2 with no bytes written

output.encoding: One byte for the highest assigned color label, followed by one byte per vertex ID in ascending order; empty input emits [0].

workspace.meaning: Fixed adjacency, active/color, component-side, queue, and first-fit tables; excludes the caller's input/output buffers and call-stack space.
